AUTHOR: Ayyagari
TITLE: Detecting Unexpected Marine Species with Underwater Cameras and Deep Learning
SPECIES: Seen: Atlantic cod, roughhead grenadier; unseen: thorny skate, redfish, striped wolffish, Atlantic halibut, spinytail skate, whelk, wolffish, unknown
DATA: DFO baited deep-sea camera videos (221 x 5-min videos); OzFish crops used as unseen-class calibration set
V_EV: Sec. I: 'Inexpensive video cameras equipped with light sources and bait were placed at depths ranging from 400 to 500 meters'
D_EV: Sec. III: 'These 221 videos were divided into train, calibration, and test splits in approximately a 70-15-15 ratio'
R_EV: Sec. III: test set 'consists of segmented fish from the seen classes within 15% of the videos in the test split' (OzFish used only for threshold calibration)
C_EV: Sec. V.C: 'optimal thresholds of 0.60 and 0.75 were calculated for the ViT and ResNet18 model' via accuracy-maximising sweep 0-1
E_EV: Table III: 'Accuracy(%) on Seen Classes ... Unseen Classes ... Entire Test Set' - classification accuracy only
ARCH: ViT, ResNet18 + kNN NNDR open-set rule
NOTE: Open-set (unseen-class reject) classification of cropped fish from deep baited cameras. Split by video for seen classes; unseen-class test crops drawn from all splits (but unseen classes never used in training). OzFish is used for threshold calibration, not as an external test -> R1 N. NIMG = total annotated crops in Table I; test set 46,641. NCLASS 3 = 2 seen + unseen. Trained with 'no pre-training'.
